previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for acute asthma exacerbation with progressive shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing. Despite initial treatment with steroids and bronchodilators, she showed limited improvement and developed radiographic evidence of right upper lobe pneumonia, prompting initiation of IV ceftriaxone and continuation of levofloxacin. She experienced transient gastrointestinal symptoms, which resolved without specific treatment, and right-sided chest pain attributed to pleuritic irritation from pneumonia rather than cardiac ischemia, as confirmed by ECG and cardiology review. Her hypertension was managed throughout, and she was discharged on a prednisone taper, antibiotics, adjusted lisinopril dosing, and new allergy medication. Smoking cessation was strongly advised given her respiratory decline, and she expressed willingness to quit. She improved clinically, with stable oxygenation and reduced work of breathing, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up instructions.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman status post right upper lobectomy for cancer.
Assess for post-op pneumothorax.

COMPARISON:  Multiple chest radiographs, most recent of ___ and
chest CT of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable AP view of the chest.

FINDINGS:  Chest tube is seen ending at the apex on the right.  No
pneumothorax is seen.  There is a density surrounding the right
paramediastinal area which is most likely due to post-operative changes.  The
remainder of the lungs appear clear.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is
normal, unchanged.  Subcutaneous air is seen in the right chest wall.  A note
is made of bilateral humeral head prostheses.

IMPRESSION:  No pneumothorax.  Right paramediastinal density most likely due
to post-operative changes.  Attention to this area on followup imaging
suggested.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with right upper lobectomy, evaluate for
pneumothorax on water seal.

COMPARISON:  Multiple chest x-ray and CTs from ___ and ___ are available for
comparison.

TECHNIQUE:  PA and lateral views of the chest are provided.

FINDINGS:  Again demonstrated a chest tube in the right hemithorax with tip at
the apical region.  There is no radiographic evidence of pneumothorax. 
Persistent right upper mediastinal widening is present and stable compared to
prior radiograph.  Cardiac silhouette appears enlarged.  The airways are
patent.  Atherosclerotic changes are demonstrated in the aorta.  The lung
fields appear clear without infiltrates or nodules.  No pleural effusions are
recognized.

IMPRESSION:  Stable appearance of the chest.  No evidence of pneumothorax.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Postop day 2 after bronchoscopy with right VATS and right
upper lobectomy.  Chest tube removed today.  Please assess for pneumothorax.

STUDY:  PA and lateral chest.

FINDINGS:

Compared to ___, the right chest tube has been removed and there is
minimal residual pneumothorax seen along the left paraspinal region and at the
lung apex medially.  This is actually smaller than when the chest tube was in.
Right lung volume is decreased from right upper lobectomy, as before.  There
is minimal left basilar atelectasis.  Heart size and mediastinal contour are
normal.

HISTORY:  Status post right VATS, now with complaint of constipation and
abdominal discomfort.  Assess for stool versus obstruction.

TECHNIQUE:  Supine and erect abdominal radiograph.

COMPARISON:  CT from ___.

FINDINGS:  There is a subcutaneous air near the right lung base, likely post-
surgical.

There is a nonspecific bowel gas pattern.  There is no evidence of obstruction
or ileus.

There are severe degenerative changes at level L4-L5, with almost complete
narrowing of the disk space, and endplate sclerosis.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of obstruction or ileus.
2.  Severe degenerative changes at level L4-L5. Please correlate clinically.

INDICATION:  ___ woman postop day 4 status post bronchoscopy, right
VATS, right upper lobectomy, now with increased right-sided chest pain. Assess
for pneumothorax or interval change.

COMPARISON:  Multiple chest radiographs, most recent ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable AP view of the chest.

FINDINGS:  Lungs remain clear bilaterally with no significant changes.  There
is a small amount of subpleural air near the right apex, unchanged. Prominence
of the right hilar region most likely represents post-surgical changes and is
stable postoperatively not concerning for increase in hematoma or fluid
collection.  Stable deviation of the trachea is due to volume loss.  Mild
cardiomegaly is stable.  Mediastinal silhouette is unchanged.

IMPRESSION:  No significant changes since prior study.  Tiny right apical
pneumothorax, unchanged.  No acute process.

These findings were discussed with ___ at the time of review on ___.

HISTORY:  Post-operative day five following video-assisted thorascopic
surgery, now with difficulty swallowing.

TECHNIQUE:  BARIUM SWALLOW

FINDINGS:  The patient initially ingested oral water-soluble contrast, to rule
out the possibility of extraluminal leak.  No leak was seen.  Following this,
the patient ingested oral barium.  The patient was unable to tolerate oral
phases and double-contrast images of the esophagus and stomach were thus
impossible.  Following oral ingestion, barium was seen to pass freely through
the esophagus into the stomach and thereafter the proximal small bowel.  There
is no fixed obstruction or stenosis.  There is no esophageal dilatation or
endoluminal filling defect.  The patient was unable to tolerate lying prone or
in the right anterior oblique position, and thus assessment of esophageal
peristaltic activity was not possible.  Following oral ingestion, a barium
tablet passed into the esophagus and remained held up just proximal to the GE
junction.  The tablet failed to pass despite a second swallow of water and
despite waiting several minutes.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Technically limited barium swallow.  No extraluminal leak, fixed
obstruction, dilatation, or hiatal hernia.  These results were discussed over
the telephone at the time of interpretation with Dr. ___ from the
surgical service.
